title: Origins and Road to War
sub: How the Croatian War of Independence began

markers.label: Zagreb
markers.description: Croatia's leadership moved from republican politics toward independence as Yugoslavia's federal order broke down.

markers.label: Knin
markers.description: The Serb Autonomous Krajina centered on Knin became the core territorial challenge to the Croatian state.

slides.title: Origins and Road to War
slides.cap: Visual reference for Origins and Road to War.
slides.body: The Croatian War of Independence grew from Yugoslavia's political collapse, Croatia's move toward sovereignty, and the refusal of Serb leaders in parts of Croatia to accept rule from Zagreb. The JNA, local Serb forces, and Croatian police all became instruments of a state crisis that turned into war.

stats.val: Origins and Road to War

title: Pakrac clash
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Pakrac
markers.description: Pakrac showed how police authority, local Serb rebellion, and federal intervention could turn administrative control into armed confrontation.

slides.title: Pakrac clash
slides.body: Pakrac was an early armed confrontation over police stations, municipal authority, and who could claim legitimacy in Serb-majority areas. It showed how quickly local institutions could become military objectives.

stats.val: Pakrac clash

title: Plitvice Lakes incident
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Plitvice Lakes
markers.description: The Easter confrontation at Plitvice produced some of the first deaths of the war and made escalation harder to reverse.

slides.title: Plitvice Lakes incident
slides.cap: Visual reference for Plitvice Lakes incident.
slides.body: The Plitvice Lakes incident, remembered as Bloody Easter, produced some of the first Croatian deaths of the war. A national park became a battlefield because control of roads, police posts, and symbols all mattered.

stats.val: Plitvice Lakes incident

title: Battle of Vukovar
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Vukovar
markers.description: Vukovar's siege became the war's central symbol of urban destruction, resistance, and civilian suffering.

slides.title: Battle of Vukovar
slides.cap: Visual reference for Battle of Vukovar.
slides.body: Vukovar endured a destructive siege by JNA and Serb forces. Its defense slowed the campaign and became a symbol of Croatian resistance, while the city's destruction and post-capture killings became central to war memory.

stats.val: Battle of Vukovar

title: Siege of Dubrovnik
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Dubrovnik
markers.description: The shelling of Dubrovnik drew international attention because a historic city far from the main front was attacked.

slides.title: Siege of Dubrovnik
slides.cap: Visual reference for Siege of Dubrovnik.
slides.body: The siege of Dubrovnik internationalized the war's image. Shelling a UNESCO-listed city damaged Croatia's heritage and made it harder for outside observers to treat the war as a distant internal Yugoslav matter.

stats.val: Siege of Dubrovnik

title: Operation Maslenica
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Maslenica Bridge area
markers.description: Croatia attacked to reopen a strategic link between Dalmatia and the rest of the country.

markers.label: Zadar hinterland
markers.description: The operation pushed front lines away from Zadar but left a tense pocket of fighting.

slides.title: Operation Maslenica
slides.body: Operation Maslenica was Croatia's attempt to restore a strategic connection to Dalmatia and push threats away from Zadar. The operation showed Croatia's army becoming more capable, but the fighting remained costly and unresolved.

stats.val: Operation Maslenica

title: Operation Medak Pocket
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Medak Pocket
markers.description: The Croatian attack reduced a Serb-held salient near Gospić but became internationally notorious for crimes against civilians and prisoners.

slides.title: Operation Medak Pocket
slides.cap: Visual reference for Operation Medak Pocket.
slides.body: Operation Medak Pocket reduced a Serb-held salient near Gospić. It also brought allegations and prosecutions over crimes against Serb civilians and prisoners, making it a military success with a heavy accountability shadow.

stats.val: Operation Medak Pocket

title: Operation Flash
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Western Slavonia
markers.description: Operation Flash rapidly retook western Slavonia and previewed Croatia's improved 1995 offensive capacity.

slides.title: Operation Flash
slides.body: Operation Flash rapidly retook western Slavonia in May 1995. It showed how far Croatian forces had developed since 1991 and signaled that frozen UN lines would not necessarily remain frozen.

stats.val: Operation Flash

title: Operation Storm
sub: Part of Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Knin
markers.description: The capture of Knin broke the political center of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

markers.label: Krajina corridors
markers.description: The offensive reopened territory while triggering a mass Serb refugee flight.

slides.title: Operation Storm
slides.body: Operation Storm broke the Republic of Serbian Krajina and restored Croatian control over most occupied territory. It also caused the flight of many Serb civilians, making victory and displacement inseparable in the war's legacy.

stats.val: Operation Storm

title: International and Human Dimensions
sub: The wider impact of the Croatian War of Independence

markers.label: Vukovar
markers.description: Vukovar anchors the human story of siege, detention, missing persons, and postwar memory.

markers.label: UN Protected Areas
markers.description: UN peacekeeping froze front lines without resolving sovereignty, displacement, or accountability.

slides.title: International and Human Dimensions
slides.cap: Visual reference for International and Human Dimensions.
slides.body: International recognition, UN peacekeeping, arms embargoes, war-crimes investigations, and refugee flows all shaped the conflict. Civilians experienced siege, expulsion, detention, missing relatives, and years of return and reconstruction.

stats.val: International and Human Dimensions

title: Outcome and Legacy
sub: How the Croatian War of Independence ended and what followed

markers.label: Eastern Slavonia
markers.description: Eastern Slavonia returned through a UN-backed transition rather than another major Croatian offensive.

markers.label: Knin
markers.description: Knin remains central to Croatian victory memory and Serbian displacement memory.

slides.title: Outcome and Legacy
slides.cap: Visual reference for Outcome and Legacy.
slides.body: Croatia secured independence and restored most territory by force, while Eastern Slavonia returned through a UN-backed transition. The legacy remains divided between liberation, loss, accountability, and unresolved memories of displacement.

stats.val: Outcome and Legacy
